$comment: The repositories the adoption workflow opens pull requests for, and the ones it must not. The order of the tiers is by how much a repository is looked at: the starred ones first, because they are the ones a visitor lands on. The exclusions carry a reason, and a repository is excluded because of what it holds, not because of what it is called: a repository that hardcodes an EORA portal or serves EORA's pages is EORA's work, whatever the name says.

excluded.eora: The EORA organisation's own introduction and plan. Not the owner's personal work.
excluded.bspb-universal-helper-poc: An EORA project: the bank's universal assistant.
excluded.projects-exporter: An EORA project: the Bitrix24 project-management dashboard, mirrored from GitLab.
excluded.outline-workspace: An EORA tool: synchronisation with the EORA wiki.
excluded.crm-exporter: An EORA tool: a Bitrix24 webhook exporter.
excluded.my-notes: The owner's notes, and they hold EORA work under Работа/EORA by their own convention.
excluded.bitrix-flow: An EORA tool: a Bitrix24 project board, pointed at the eora.bitrix24.ru portal.
excluded.monos-home: A home server for EORA's services.
excluded.wiki-js: EORA's internal wiki, kept as pages in Git. A Wiki.js instance serves it and writes every edit back.
